lesson.text: Remember? Words are built from roots, prefixes and suffixes. Spelling rules tell us what happens when we add endings, and word families help us spell whole groups of words.
Word families share a spelling pattern: night, light, right, bright (-ight). Station, action, fraction (-tion, said "shun").
Adding -ing or -ed to a short word that ends in one vowel and one consonant? Double the last letter: hop, hopping; run, running; stop, stopped.
A word ending in e? Drop the e: make, making; smile, smiled. A consonant and then y? Change the y to i before -ed or -es: cry, cried, cries. Keep the y before -ing: crying.
Some tricky words must be learned by heart: because, friend, said, people, answer, believe, different, important. Look, say, cover, write, check!
To check a spelling, use a dictionary. Its words are in alphabetical order: look at the first letter, then the second. Bat comes before bee, because a comes before e.
Try it in the world: write a sign in your world with three -ight words: "A bright light at night!" Then check each spelling. Next: nouns and pronouns.

exercises.prompt: Which word has the same spelling pattern as "night"?
exercises.explain: Night and light both end in -ight. Kite and bite rhyme but are spelled differently.

exercises.hint: Short word, one vowel, one consonant: double it.
exercises.explain: run ends in one vowel and one consonant, so double the n: running.

exercises.prompt: Which word comes first in a dictionary?
exercises.explain: a comes before b and c, so apple comes first.
Drop the e, then add -ing: making.

exercises.hint: A consonant and then y: change the y.
exercises.explain: Change y to i and add -ed: cried.

exercises.prompt: Zara writes a note to her best ___. Which spelling is correct?
exercises.hint: It has the word end at the end.
exercises.explain: fr-i-end: friend. It has end at the end.

exercises.prompt: Put these b words in alphabetical order.
exercises.hint: They all start with b, so look at the second letter.
exercises.explain: a, e, i, u: bat, bee, bird, bus.

exercises.hint: One vowel, one consonant at the end.
exercises.explain: Double the p, then add -ed: stopped.

exercises.prompt: "My twin and I have ___ hobbies." Which spelling is correct?
Put these c words in alphabetical order.
exercises.hint: Same first letter? Look at the second.
exercises.explain: a, h, l, r: cat, chair, cloud, crab.

exercises.prompt: Why is there a double p in "hopping"?
choices: Hop has one short vowel and one last consonant
exercises.explain: Hop ends in one vowel and one consonant, so the p doubles before -ing.

exercises.hint: Think: never believe a lie. There is a lie in believe.
exercises.explain: False: it is b-e-l-i-e-v-e. There is a lie in believe!

exercises.prompt: Sort the words by their spelling pattern.
exercises.hint: Look at the ends of the words.
exercises.explain: Night and bright end in -ight; station and action end in -tion.

exercises.hint: One vowel and then one consonant at the end? Double it.
exercises.explain: Hopping and running double the letter. Jumping and playing just add -ing.

exercises.prompt: Add -ing: sort the words by what happens first.
exercises.hint: One vowel and one consonant at the end? A word ending in e? Neither?
exercises.explain: Double it: swimming, stopping (one vowel, one consonant). Drop the e: smiling, baking. Just add -ing: jumping, playing.

exercises.prompt: Add -ed to each word. Match it to its spelling.
exercises.hint: Check each word's ending: a consonant and y, one vowel and one consonant, an e, or a vowel and y?
exercises.explain: Cry ends in a consonant and y, so the y turns to i: cried. Hop doubles its p: hopped. Smile ends in e, so just add d: smiled. Play has a vowel before the y, so it keeps it: played.
